- `main` is clean and synchronized with `origin/main`.

- Validation is unusually thorough, including strong coverage floors, Chromium/mobile/WebKit journeys, deployment identity checks, bounded rate limiting, sanitized logging, and privacy-safe analytics.

## Recommended first PR

`docs(repo): refresh project front door`

1. Replace the obsolete image

   [display.png](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/my-first-commit/display.png) comes from the initial implementation and depicts a profile/bio interface the app no longer renders.

   Replace it with one accurate, optimized screenshot of the current results experience:

   - Store it under `docs/assets/my-first-commit-results.png`.
   - Capture a polished desktop viewport with a real public example.
   - Keep meaningful alt text.
   - Delete `display.png`.
   - Use a real product screenshot, not generated artwork. The existing Open Graph artwork already handles promotional imagery.

2. Simplify the README

   [README.md](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/my-first-commit/README.md:1) currently repeats its link directory and includes detailed architecture, privacy, stack, and limitation content.

   Keep the README as the front door:

   - Product name and one-sentence value proposition
   - Badges
   - Live-app link
   - Current screenshot
   - Four or five core capabilities
   - Minimal local quick start
   - Compact documentation table
   - Contributing, contributors, and license links

   Move the detailed features and limitations into a new `docs/product.md`. Link architecture, privacy, operations, testing, and releases to the existing specialized documents. This follows GitHub’s recommendation that a README explain usefulness and getting started while longer material lives elsewhere. [GitHub README guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-readmes)

3. Improve the badge row

   The build and production badges already exist and are accurate. I recommend:

   - CI
   - Production Health
   - Latest stable release
   - MIT license
   - Vercel/live app

   Move the static Next.js and Node.js badges into the technology documentation or remove them; they are stack labels, not health signals, and can drift. Do not add a coverage badge unless coverage is actually published to a service such as Codecov.

4. Add `CONTRIBUTORS.md`

   Start simply:

   - Scott Densmore as creator and maintainer
   - A thank-you to human contributors
   - Link to GitHub’s contributor history
   - A note explaining how contributions are recognized

   I would not list Dependabot as a person or add All Contributors automation yet.

5. Keep the MIT license

   [LICENSE](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/my-first-commit/LICENSE:1) is the standard MIT text, has the correct copyright holder/year, and GitHub recognizes it as MIT. It makes sense for a public portfolio-style app intended to permit reuse. MIT requires preservation of its copyright and license notice and disclaims warranty. [MIT license summary](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/mit/)

   Don’t modify the standard license body. Change the README’s plain `MIT` text into a link to the license. If future artwork contains third-party material, document that separately rather than altering MIT.

## Follow-up PRs

After the front-door PR:

- Add `SECURITY.md`, a pull-request template, and optionally a standard code of conduct. GitHub currently reports only 57% community-profile completeness; these files would improve contributor expectations and responsible vulnerability reporting. [GitHub community-profile guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/about-community-profiles-for-public-repositories)
- Add `description`, `homepage`, `repository`, `bugs`, and `"license": "MIT"` to [package.json](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/my-first-commit/package.json:1).
- Treat CSP enforcement as a separate security project. It is intentionally report-only today and still permits inline scripts/eval in [next.config.ts](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/my-first-commit/next.config.ts:24). Enforcing it safely needs production-report review and dedicated testing.

My recommendation is to implement the front-door PR first as one coherent, reviewable slice, including the README, current screenshot, `docs/product.md`, `CONTRIBUTORS.md`, badge cleanup, and changelog entry.

+# Product Guide
+
+My First Commit turns GitHub's public commit search into a small origin story. A visitor enters a
+GitHub username and sees the earliest public commit GitHub can find, followed by the next nine
+results in chronological order.
+
+## Product Principles
+
+- **Focused:** one search task, without accounts, profiles, feeds, or a database.
+- **Honest:** partial or unavailable GitHub results are described as such rather than presented as
+  authoritative history.
+- **Recoverable:** empty results, rate limits, timeouts, and upstream failures offer a useful next
+  action.
+- **Private by default:** recent searches stay in the browser, and searched usernames are excluded
+  from analytics properties and analytics URLs.
+- **Shareable:** a search can be sent as a URL or copied as a compact text summary.
+
+## Capabilities
+
+### Origin discovery
+
+The app searches GitHub's public commit index by author, orders results from oldest to newest, and
+requests the first ten matches. The first result receives a detailed summary; the following results
+form the rest of the timeline.
+
+### Search shortcuts
+
+Known public profiles provide examples for a first visit and recovery from an empty result. After a
+successful search, up to five recent usernames are kept in the visitor's browser as shortcuts. They
+can be rerun or cleared without creating an account.
+
+### Sharing
+
+A completed search updates the page URL with the username. Opening that URL starts the same search,
+and a copy action creates a short result summary with links back to the search and earliest commit.
+
+### Failure handling
+
+Validation errors, empty searches, rate limits, timeouts, GitHub outages, and unexpected failures
+have distinct messages and recovery paths. When GitHub marks a search incomplete, the app labels
+the timeline as partial, does not cache it, and offers another search without discarding the visible
+results if that retry fails.
+
+### Production visibility
+
+The footer identifies the deployed release. GitHub Actions validates each change, a production
+browser check exercises healthy deployments, and a release is promoted only after the deployed
+commit passes both checks.
+
+## Data and Privacy
+
+- A searched username is sent to GitHub to retrieve public commit data.
+- `GITHUB_TOKEN`, when configured, is used only by the server and is never exposed to the browser.
+- Recent searches are stored in browser `localStorage` under
+  `my-first-commit:recent-searches`.
+- Successful and empty search results may be cached briefly in one server process to reduce
+  repeated GitHub API calls. The cache is temporary and is not durable storage.
+- Vercel Analytics receives product-health events without the searched username. Shared-search
+  parameters are removed from analytics URLs before they are sent.
+- The app has no accounts, database, or app-owned server-side search history.
+
+The live [privacy page](https://my-first-commit-eta.vercel.app/privacy) is the visitor-facing notice.
+The [architecture guide](architecture.md#data-boundaries) describes the implementation boundaries,
+and the [production runbook](production.md#privacy-and-local-storage) covers operational details.
+
+## Limitations
+
+“First commit” means the earliest public commit GitHub's current search index returns for an author.
+It is not a complete or immutable record of everything that person has authored.
+
+- Only public commits indexed by GitHub are searchable. Private commits, deleted repositories, and
+  private forks are not included.
+- GitHub's index can lag behind new pushes, omit older history, or return the same commit through
+  forks and mirrors.
+- Squashed, rebased, rewritten, or force-pushed history can change the earliest visible result.
+- Renamed accounts, changed author emails, bot-authored commits, and missing author metadata can
+  affect which commits match a username.
+- GitHub may return an incomplete result when a search takes too long. The app labels that result as
+  partial rather than claiming it found the definitive first commit.
+- Unauthenticated requests have stricter rate limits. A server-side token improves reliability but
+  does not make private data searchable.
+
+## Technology
+
+My First Commit is a Next.js App Router application built with React, strict TypeScript, Tailwind
+CSS, Octokit, and Vercel Analytics. It uses the visitor's system fonts and generated metadata images,
+so builds do not depend on a font or image host. See the [architecture guide](architecture.md) for
+the request flow and the [development guide](development.md) for the supported runtime and commands.
